summary.text: 東 means “east,” but its early shape is explained in the supplied modern accounts as a bag, basket, or tied bundle. The character was borrowed to write the word for “east.” The familiar image of a sun rising behind a tree reflects a different, traditional interpretation of the shape.

history.text: The Shuowen records an interpretation involving the sun within a tree. Wiktionary argues that the early form differs enough to make such tree-based explanations doubtful. Its alternatives include a bag tied at both ends and a form connected with 束 or 橐, while Dong Chinese gives the broader basket-or-bag account.

uncertainties.text: The original object and the precise graphic relationship to other characters are disputed. The excerpts support distinguishing those object-based proposals from the later sun-and-tree interpretation, but do not establish one exact reconstruction.
